classification.difficultyReason: Determine Danielle's displacement from Christos in each arrangement, choose an inverse-tangent ratio and adjust the reference angle to the correct bearing quadrant.

content.prompt: Christos is $200\text{ m}$ from a tree and Danielle is $400\text{ m}$ from the same tree. What is the bearing of Danielle from Christos, to the nearest degree, if:

children.label: a
children.prompt: Christos is due north of the tree and Danielle is due east of the tree?

answer.short:
$117^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$

Use inverse tangent to find the angle south of east, then add $90^{\circ}$.
answer.worked:
From Christos, Danielle is $400\text{ m}$ east and $200\text{ m}$ south. Let $\theta$ be the angle south of east.

$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{200}{400}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac12\right)\\\theta&\approx26.565^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

The bearing is measured clockwise from north.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing}&=90^{\circ}+\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac12\right)\\\text{Bearing}&\approx117^{\circ}\mathrm{T}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Christos is due west of the tree and Danielle is due south of the tree?

answer.short:
$153^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$

Use inverse tangent to find the angle east of south, then subtract it from $180^{\circ}$.
answer.worked:
From Christos, Danielle is $200\text{ m}$ east and $400\text{ m}$ south. Let $\theta$ be the angle east of south.

$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{200}{400}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac12\right)\\\theta&\approx26.565^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

The bearing is measured clockwise from north.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing}&=180^{\circ}-\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac12\right)\\\text{Bearing}&\approx153^{\circ}\mathrm{T}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Christos is due east of the tree and Danielle is due south of the tree?

answer.short:
$207^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$

Use inverse tangent to find the angle west of south, then add $180^{\circ}$.
answer.worked:
From Christos, Danielle is $200\text{ m}$ west and $400\text{ m}$ south. Let $\theta$ be the angle west of south.

$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{200}{400}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac12\right)\\\theta&\approx26.565^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

The bearing is measured clockwise from north.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing}&=180^{\circ}+\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac12\right)\\\text{Bearing}&\approx207^{\circ}\mathrm{T}\end{align*}$$
